limitations: M25-0016-P1 — Integral fundamental-cycle normalization — Counterevidence: Torsion-free groups work; rational normalization works after inverting torsion order.
M25-0016-P2 — Refined isogeny comparison omits degree — Counterevidence: Connection and moment diagrams account for their own factors but not the inserted top form.
M25-0016-P3 — Wrong binomial sign in explicit current — Counterevidence: Moment zero misses the defect; inserting (-1)^b repairs the local inverse.

M25-0016-P4 — Translation duplicates full residue pullback — Counterevidence: Weighted residue proof works with the function on a single c-torsion component extended by zero, not the full inverse image.
M25-0016-P5 — Wrong units in ray-class kernel — Counterevidence: Full-unit quotient is correct for trivial tame conductor in Step 3.
M25-0016-P6 — Weight invariants require torsion-free module — Counterevidence: Later differential modules are locally free over a domain.
M25-0016-P7 — Completed and uncompleted residues confused — Counterevidence: Mellin proof and later current formulas use completion.
M25-0016-P8 — Subgroup change ignores coset stabilizer — Counterevidence: Fixed torsion coset gives original index; full orbit sums may restore aggregate factor.
M25-0016-P9 — Universal critical-value nonvanishing false — Counterevidence: Period comparison remains a nonzero-period comparison; Theorem4.10 allows zero.
M25-0016-P10 — Injective descent need not be flabby — Counterevidence: Borel comparison itself holds; coinduced module is acyclic and difference equation solvable.

proposition.claim:
The CM type of \(L\) is lifted as specified in Section 1.1, and \(2d=[L:\mathbb Q]\). The base \(R\) is an \(\mathcal O_{L^{\rm Gal}}[1/d_L]\)-algebra contained in \(\mathbb C\) when integral specializations are used. A characteristic-zero domain need not contain the inverse of every integer. Critical Hecke type is \(\mu=\beta-\alpha\), with \(\alpha\geq\mathbf1\); derivative indices instead use \(\mu=\beta-\alpha-\mathbf1\), with \(\alpha,\beta\geq0\). These conventions must not be conflated.

The finite-index subgroup \(\Gamma\subset\mathcal O_L^\times\) is not everywhere torsion-free. Sections 3.2, 3.4 and the opening of Section 5 impose that condition; later congruence unit groups can have torsion. The original integral class requires the specified isogeny and its dual to be etale. Section 2.5 deliberately removes invertibility of \(N\mathfrak f\), which matters in Problem 2. Ordinary \(p\)-adic arguments require \(p\nmid d_L\), disjoint CM prime sets, and an initial point of order prime to \(p\). A generic-fiber identity alone does not establish integral descent.

Relevant dependencies in the manuscript are \[\begin{gathered}
2.20\longrightarrow2.27,\ 2.28\longrightarrow
3.20,\ 3.22,\ 3.23,\ 3.27\longrightarrow4.9\longrightarrow4.10,\\
2.30,\ 2.31\longrightarrow4.9,\qquad
5.9,\ 5.11,\ 5.15\longrightarrow5.22\longrightarrow5.23
\longrightarrow5.25\longrightarrow5.27.
\end{gathered}\] This records uses, not their validity. Trace duality and finite Fourier orthogonality have the expected behavior with the unramified hypothesis. Boundary cases checked below include \(d=1\), finite unit groups, zero derivative degree, zero translation, zero critical \(L\)-value, and trivial versus nontrivial tame conductor.

repair.content:
Restrict to torsion-free groups or invert torsion order, then re-establish descent.

Restore degree in rational comparison; integral construction requires more than dividing by a nonunit.

Insert alternating binomial sign and recompute holomorphic derivative and volume conventions.

Replace right-side f' by component-supported f0 and redo pairing/local-factor checks.

Use closure of O_f^* consistently in G, q and pushforward, then redo interpolation.

Add R-torsion-free hypothesis or weightwise annihilator condition.

State pole and residue claims for completed function.

Use [Gamma_t:Gamma_t intersect Gamma'] or add fixed-coset hypothesis.

Replace Qbar^* by Qbar for L-value or assume nonvanishing.

Use acyclicity and descent/Cartan-Leray argument.
